l1: What Windows version is the affected system running? (Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName,OsVersion,OsBuildNumber)
Is the proxy configuration manual (static), automatic (PAC/WPAD), or using no proxy?
Are you troubleshooting browser issues, application connectivity issues, or Windows Update failures?
Is the system using a corporate proxy server or direct internet connection?
Are multiple browsers or applications affected, or just one specific application?
Is the system domain-joined or standalone? Domain GPO may be pushing proxy settings.
l2: Which proxy client stack is the affected application using? WinInet (Internet Explorer/Edge Classic), WinHTTP (Windows Update, services), or custom proxy implementation?
Is WPAD (Web Proxy Auto-Discovery) configured? Check with 'netsh winhttp show proxy' — WPAD uses DHCP option 252 or DNS wpad.domain.local.
Is a PAC (Proxy Auto-Configuration) file configured? Check with 'netsh winhttp show proxy' — PAC file contains JavaScript for proxy routing logic.
Are proxy authentication credentials configured? Applications may fail if proxy requires authentication and credentials are missing or expired.
Is the proxy server reachable? Test with 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <proxy_host> -Port <proxy_port>' — typically TCP 8080, 3128, or 443.
Are SSL/TLS inspection or HTTPS interception configured on the proxy? This can cause certificate trust issues.
Is IPv6 proxy configuration present alongside IPv4? Dual-stack environments may have conflicting proxy settings.
Are bypass lists configured? Check 'netsh winhttp show proxy' — bypass list includes sites that should connect directly.
Is the issue intermittent or persistent? Intermittent issues may indicate proxy server load balancing or health issues.
Are WinHTTP proxy settings different from WinInet settings? Applications using different stacks may have inconsistent proxy behavior.

l1: Check WinHTTP proxy settings: 'netsh winhttp show proxy' — displays current WinHTTP proxy configuration used by Windows services.
Check WinInet proxy settings: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Select ProxyEnable,ProxyServer' — displays browser proxy settings.
Check automatic proxy detection: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Select AutoDetect,AutoConfigURL' — displays WPAD and PAC configuration.
Test proxy server connectivity: 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <proxy_host> -Port <proxy_port>' — verify proxy server is reachable.
Test direct connectivity (bypass proxy): 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <target> -Port 443' — verify internet is reachable without proxy.
Check proxy authentication: Applications may prompt for credentials or fail with 407 Proxy Authentication Required.
l2: Export complete WinHTTP configuration: 'netsh winhttp dump > C:\winhttp_config.txt' — review all WinHTTP proxy settings.
Export WinInet proxy settings: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Out-File C:\wininet_settings.txt' — review browser proxy configuration.

Check proxy bypass list: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Select ProxyOverride' — verify bypass list includes local addresses and intranet sites.
Check system-wide proxy settings: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Select ProxyEnable,ProxyServer' — system-level proxy configuration.
Check WPAD DNS resolution: 'Resolve-DnsName -Name wpad.<domain> -Type A' — verify WPAD host can be resolved.
Check PAC file accessibility: 'Invoke-WebRequest -Uri <pac_url> -UseBasicParsing' — verify PAC file can be downloaded.

Check proxy authentication via registry: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Select ProxyUser,ProxyPass' — if credentials are stored (not recommended).
Check proxy configuration for specific application: Application-specific proxy settings may be in app config files or registry.
Check network adapter proxy settings: 'Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq Up | Select Name' — verify adapter-specific proxy configuration if present.
Test with proxy temporarily disabled: 'netsh winhttp reset proxy' — resets WinHTTP to direct connection, retest, then restore.
Capture network trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-WinHTTP level=5 tracefile=C:\winhttp_trace.etl' — reproduce issue, then 'netsh trace stop'.

l1: If WinHTTP proxy is misconfigured: Reset with 'netsh winhttp reset proxy' — clears WinHTTP proxy settings, then configure correctly with 'netsh winhttp set proxy <proxy_server>:<port>'.
If WinInet proxy is blocking: Disable temporarily via Internet Options > Connections > LAN Settings > uncheck 'Use a proxy server' — retest, then re-enable.
If WPAD is not working: Disable automatic detection via Internet Options > Connections > LAN Settings > uncheck 'Automatically detect settings' — configure proxy manually.
If PAC file is not loading: Verify PAC URL is correct and accessible — check with 'Invoke-WebRequest -Uri <pac_url>'.
If proxy server is unreachable: Check network connectivity and DNS resolution to proxy host — verify proxy server is online.
If proxy authentication fails: Verify credentials are correct — use domain credentials if proxy is domain-integrated.
l2: If WinHTTP and WinInet settings are inconsistent: Sync them manually — set WinHTTP to match WinInet with 'netsh winhttp import proxy source=ie'.
If bypass list is not working: Add bypass entries via Internet Options > Connections > LAN Settings > Advanced > add exceptions for local addresses, intranet sites.
If WPAD DNS resolution fails: Check DHCP option 252 configuration on DHCP server — verify wpad.domain.local DNS record exists.
If PAC file has syntax errors: Validate PAC file syntax using browser developer tools or online PAC file validators — fix JavaScript errors.
If proxy SSL inspection breaks certificates: Add proxy CA certificate to Trusted Root CAs via 'certutil -addstore Root <ca_cert.cer>' — or disable SSL inspection on proxy.
If IPv6 proxy is not working: Verify proxy server supports IPv6 — configure IPv6 proxy address in proxy settings.
If application ignores proxy settings: Application may be using custom proxy implementation — check application configuration for proxy settings.

If GPO is pushing incorrect proxy settings: Check applied GPO with 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_report.html' — review Computer/User Configuration > Windows Settings > Internet Explorer Maintenance > Connection.
If proxy authentication fails for services: Configure service account credentials in Credential Manager or use GPO to pass service credentials to proxy.
If WinHTTP proxy is not applied to services: Restart services after changing WinHTTP settings — 'Restart-Service wuauserv' for Windows Update.

l1: Export WinHTTP proxy settings: 'netsh winhttp show proxy > C:\winhttp_proxy.txt'
Export WinInet proxy settings: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Out-File C:\wininet_proxy.txt'
Export system proxy settings: 'Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" | Out-File C:\system_proxy.txt'
Export network adapter configuration: 'Get-NetAdapter | Export-Csv C:\network_adapters.csv -NoTypeInformation'
l2: Export complete WinHTTP configuration: 'netsh winhttp dump > C:\winhttp_dump.txt'
Export WinInet registry settings: 'reg export "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" C:\wininet_registry.reg'
Export system proxy registry: 'reg export "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings" C:\system_proxy_registry.reg'
Export WinHTTP registry: 'reg export "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings\Connections" C:\winhttp_registry.reg'
Export WPAD/DHCP configuration: 'ipconfig /all > C:\ipconfig.txt' — check for WPAD configuration.
Test PAC file download: 'Invoke-WebRequest -Uri <pac_url> -OutFile C:\pac_file.js -UseBasicParsing' — save PAC file for analysis.
Export browser proxy settings: Check Edge/Chrome proxy settings via Settings > System > Proxy or browser-specific configurations.
Export Credential Manager proxy credentials: 'cmdkey /list > C:\credential_manager.txt' — check for stored proxy credentials.
Export GPO proxy settings: 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_report.html' — review proxy-related GPO configuration.

Export Windows Update logs: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName "Microsoft-Windows-WindowsUpdateClient/Operational" -MaxEvents 50 | Out-File C:\windows_update_logs.txt' — check for proxy-related Windows Update failures.
Export Application event log: 'wevtutil epl Application C:\app_events.evtx' — contains application proxy failures.
Export System event log: 'wevtutil epl System C:\system_events.evtx' — contains system-level proxy events.
Capture WinHTTP ETL trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-WinHTTP level=5 tracefile=C:\winhttp_trace.etl' — reproduce issue — 'netsh trace stop'.
Test proxy server connectivity: 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <proxy_host> -Port <proxy_port> -InformationLevel Detailed > C:\proxy_connectivity.txt'.
TSS data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_Proxy' — collects comprehensive proxy diagnostics including WinHTTP, Winsock, NCSI, WebIO, and network state traces.
